title: Top Michelin Star Restaurants in the World (2026 Ranking)
description: The world’s top Michelin star restaurants, ranked by their places on The World’s 50 Best, OAD and La Liste: the top 50, the best three-stars and more.
h1: Top Michelin Star Restaurants in the World
summary: The starred restaurants the critics rate highest, ranked across The World’s 50 Best Restaurants, OAD and La Liste, with what a meal costs.

picks.text: Dabiz Muñoz’s restaurant in Madrid is known for its theatrical tasting menu, which throws Spanish, Chinese, Japanese and Mexican flavors together, served in a dining room in the NH Collection Eurobuilding hotel. The half menu is the cheaper way in.

Jorge Vallejo and his wife Alejandra Flores run this dining room in Polanco, where Mexican produce is cooked with a light, modern hand. It holds two stars in the MICHELIN Guide Mexico and is No. 3 on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025.

Chef Supaksorn ‘Ice’ Jongsiri cooks the food of southern Thailand in a house in Bangkok, with ingredients from small producers in the south. It holds three stars, and OAD’s 2026 Asia list puts it at No. 1. Prices are “++”: service and VAT come on top.

Bittor Arguinzoniz grills almost everything over wood in a stone house in Axpe, a hamlet in the hills of Bizkaia. Michelin gives it one star; the critics put it at No. 2 on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025 and No. 1 on OAD’s 2026 Europe list. It serves lunch only.

Norbert Niederkofler’s restaurant in Brunico, South Tyrol, cooks only what comes from the surrounding mountains, an approach he calls “Cook the Mountain”. It holds three stars and scores 99 out of 100 in La Liste.

Junghyun and Ellia Park’s Korean tasting menu in NoMad, New York, is served at a counter, with a card for every course explaining what’s on the plate. Two stars, No. 12 on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025 and No. 7 on North America’s 50 Best 2026.

Bruno Verjus, a food writer who taught himself to cook, serves produce from small farms and fishermen at Table, near the Gare de Lyon in Paris. It holds two stars and is No. 8 on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025, but it closes for good on 22 December 2026, as Verjus announced in September.

Julien Royer’s French restaurant in the National Gallery Singapore is named after his grandmother. It holds three stars, and La Liste gives it 97.5 out of 100. Prices are “++”: service and GST come on top.

Niko Romito cooks pared-back Italian food at Casadonna, a restored former monastery above Castel di Sangro in the mountains of Abruzzo. It holds three stars and is No. 18 on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025.
Twin brothers Thomas and Mathias Sühring cook modern German food, much of it from family recipes, in a villa with a garden in Bangkok. It holds three stars, and La Liste gives it 96 out of 100.

body:
The top Michelin star restaurant in the world on the critics’ lists is {{acTop}} in {{acTopPlace}}, a {{acTopStars}}-star restaurant that {{acTopLists}}. We ranked every one of the world’s {{total}} starred restaurants by its places on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants, OAD and La Liste; {{acN}} appear on at least one.

The MICHELIN Guide doesn’t rank its restaurants beyond giving them one, two or three stars. Three other lists do, each in its own way: The World’s 50 Best Restaurants by a vote of chefs, critics and food writers, OAD by the ratings of thousands of well-traveled diners, and La Liste by scoring restaurants out of 100 from guides and reviews worldwide. A restaurant that does well on all three is one the critics agree on, so we combined them into one Michelin star restaurants world ranking: the best Michelin star restaurants in the world, as the critics see them. For what the stars themselves mean, see What is a Michelin star?

Top 10Top 50Best three-starBy starsUnder {{valueUSD}}By countryHow we ranked them

The top 10 Michelin star restaurants in the world

The ten starred restaurants with the strongest places across the critics’ lists come from seven countries on three continents, from a lunch-only grill in the Basque hills to Korean, southern Thai and modern Mexican tasting menus. Six hold three stars, but the critics and the MICHELIN Guide don’t always agree: Etxebarri, with one star, is No. 2 on The World’s 50 Best.

{{table:acclaimed-top10}}

Top 50 Michelin star restaurants in the world

Of the top 50, {{ac50Three}} hold three stars, {{ac50Two}} two and {{ac50One}} one, across {{ac50Countries}} countries, led by {{ac50Lead}} ({{ac50LeadN}}). Bangkok does especially well, as its best restaurants feature on The World’s 50 Best, Asia’s 50 Best and La Liste alike, and so does Italy, whose three-star restaurants score highly with La Liste and OAD. The famous names are here too: Arpège in Paris, Steirereck in Vienna and Le Bernardin in New York.

{{table:acclaimed-50}}

Best 3 Michelin star restaurants in the world

Three stars is the highest Michelin star rating, held by {{n3}} restaurants, and {{ac3N}} of them appear on at least one critics’ list. On the critics’ lists, the best is {{ac3Top}} in {{ac3TopPlace}}, followed by restaurants in Thailand, Italy, Singapore and South Korea. Expect to pay {{range3}} per person for dinner at a three-star restaurant, before drinks and service. For every one of them, country by country, see every 3 Michelin star restaurant in the world.

{{table:acclaimed-3}}

The most acclaimed restaurants at two stars and one star

Three-star restaurants fill much of the overall ranking, so here are the 10 most acclaimed at the other two levels.

Most acclaimed 2 Michelin star restaurants

{{ac2Top}} in {{ac2TopPlace}} leads the two-star list. Several here are on The World’s 50 Best but have stayed at two stars, among them Atomix in New York, Table in Paris and Narisawa in Tokyo.

{{table:acclaimed-2}}

Most acclaimed 1 Michelin star restaurants

{{ac1Top}} leads the one-star list, and {{ac1N}} one-star restaurants appear on a critics’ list in all. Bangkok’s Gaggan and Potong, Buenos Aires steakhouse Don Julio and Hong Kong’s The Chairman are among the world’s most celebrated restaurants with a single star.

{{table:acclaimed-1}}

The most acclaimed Michelin star restaurants for under {{valueUSD}}

{{acValueN}} of the critics’ picks have a meal for {{valueUSD}} or less per person, usually a set lunch or a meal à la carte. These are the 10 most acclaimed, with the cheapest way in. The most affordable Michelin star restaurants of all, street-food stalls and roast-meat shops in Singapore, Hong Kong and Bangkok, rarely appear on these lists: see the cheapest Michelin star restaurants in the world.

To find one that fits your own budget and dates, try Help me pick, or see what’s around you with Near me.

{{table:acclaimed-value}}

The most acclaimed Michelin star restaurant in every country

The critics’ favorite in each of the {{acCountries}} countries and territories with a starred restaurant on at least one list. Tap a column heading to sort. For how many starred restaurants each country has, see Michelin star restaurants by country.

{{table:acclaimed-countries}}

How we ranked them

Every restaurant here holds stars in the current MICHELIN Guide editions. Its place in our ranking comes from the latest edition of three families of critics’ lists, each taken from the list’s own website in {{acChecked}}: The World’s 50 Best Restaurants (with its 51–100 list) and its regional lists for Asia, North America, Latin America and the Middle East and North Africa; OAD’s Top Restaurants for Europe, North America, Asia, Japan and South America; and La Liste’s Top 1000.

Each family gives points for a restaurant’s best place on it. The World’s 50 Best gives 60 for No. 1 down to 10 for No. 100, and a regional 50 Best 40 down to 10; a restaurant on both counts only its better place, so restaurants outside Europe, which has no regional list, don’t count twice. OAD gives 40 for No. 1 down to nothing at No. 600, and La Liste gives its score above 70. The points add up, and ties go to the restaurant with more stars.

The lists change every year. The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2026 is announced in November 2026, and La Liste 2027 later that month; we update this list of the best Michelin star restaurants (2026 edition) after each, and after each MICHELIN Guide ceremony, as stars are won and lost. Until October 2026 we ranked starred restaurants by their Google reviews instead; Google’s terms don’t allow us to keep its ratings, so we now link to them. Prices are per person, before drinks and service, in local currency with US dollars at recent exchange rates.

faq.q: What is the top Michelin star restaurant in the world?
faq.a: The MICHELIN Guide doesn’t rank restaurants beyond one, two or three stars, so there is no official number one. Across the critics’ lists (The World’s 50 Best Restaurants, OAD and La Liste), the top starred restaurant is {{acTop}} in {{acTopPlace}}, which {{acTopLists}}.

faq.q: What is the highest rated Michelin star restaurant in the world?
faq.a: La Liste, which scores restaurants out of 100, gives its top score of 99.5 to several starred restaurants, among them Le Bernardin in New York, SingleThread in California, Martín Berasategui near San Sebastián and Da Vittorio near Bergamo. On The World’s 50 Best Restaurants 2025, the highest placed with Michelin stars is Etxebarri in the Basque Country, at No. 2.

faq.q: What are the most famous Michelin star restaurants in the world?
faq.a: Fame is hard to measure, but the restaurants the critics’ lists agree on are a fair guide: {{acTop}}, Quintonil in Mexico City, Etxebarri in the Basque Country, Gaggan in Bangkok, Le Bernardin in New York and Arpège in Paris are all near the top of our ranking.

faq.q: How much does a meal at a top Michelin star restaurant cost?
faq.a: A dinner tasting menu typically costs about {{price1}} per person at a one-star restaurant, {{price2}} at two stars and {{price3}} at three stars, before drinks and service. Many of the most acclaimed have a cheaper set lunch, and {{acValueN}} of them have a meal for {{valueUSD}} or less.

faq.q: Why isn’t the world’s best restaurant on this list?
faq.a: Some restaurants at the top of The World’s 50 Best have no Michelin stars, because the MICHELIN Guide doesn’t cover their country: Maido in Lima, No. 1 on the 2025 list, is one. This ranking includes only restaurants with stars in the current MICHELIN Guide editions.
